title: Biomolecules
summary: Which molecules are living things made of, and what do they do?
cards.0.p: Water makes up about 70% of a cell's mass. It dissolves substances and keeps body temperature steady. Minerals give no energy but regulate processes in the body. Water and minerals are inorganic substances. The other biomolecules, which have a carbon skeleton, are organic.
cards.0.key: Water, minerals and vitamins are absorbed without being digested. A living thing takes in water and minerals ready-made from outside.
cards.0.once.soru: When you sweat, you lose water and salt (minerals). Do minerals give the body energy?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Minerals give no energy. They play a regulating role. For example, calcium is needed for bones, iron for hemoglobin, and sodium and potassium for nerve signals.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Energy comes from carbohydrates, fats and proteins. Minerals are regulators.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Minerals give no energy at all. Their job is to regulate processes in the body.
cards.1.h: Water leaves as units join, and enters as they split
cards.1.p: Small units (monomers) join to form large molecules (polymers). Water is released as they join, and this is called dehydration synthesis. In the reverse, water is added and the bond breaks. This is called hydrolysis. Digestion is hydrolysis.
cards.1.svg#5: Water is released as units join and used as they split
cards.1.key: In dehydration, units join and water is released. In hydrolysis, water is added and the bond breaks.
cards.2.p: Carbohydrates are made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, and they are a living thing's first choice of energy source. Glucose, fructose, galactose, ribose and deoxyribose are monosaccharides. When two monosaccharides join, a disaccharide forms: maltose, sucrose and lactose.
cards.2.key: All three of these disaccharides contain glucose.
cards.2.once.soru: Table sugar (sucrose) forms when two small sugars join. What is released as they join?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: One water molecule is released in each join: glucose + fructose → sucrose + water. When two monosaccharides join, a disaccharide forms.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: CO₂ is released when sugars are burned in respiration, not when they join.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: The molecule that leaves during the join is water, not oxygen.
cards.3.p: Many glucose molecules join to form polysaccharides. Starch is the storage form in plants, and glycogen in animals. Cellulose makes up plant cell walls, and humans cannot digest it. Chitin is a polysaccharide that makes up the exoskeleton of insects.
cards.3.key: Glycogen is highly branched. So glucose can be cut from many ends at once, and energy is supplied fast.
cards.4.p: Lipids do not dissolve in water. A fat molecule (triglyceride) is made of 1 glycerol and 3 fatty acids. A gram of fat gives more than twice the energy of a gram of carbohydrate. That is why fat is used for long-term storage, and it also insulates the body against cold.
cards.4.key: Breaking down fat also releases more metabolic water than carbohydrate does. Camels and hibernating animals use this water.
cards.5.p: In saturated fatty acids, there are only single bonds between the carbons. Their chains are straight, so they pack tightly. That is why butter is solid. In unsaturated fatty acids, a double bond bends the chain. Bent chains cannot pack tightly. That is why olive oil is liquid.
cards.5.svg#8: Essential fatty acids must come from food
cards.5.key: Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids are essential. The body cannot make them, so we must get them from food.
cards.5.once.soru: Butter is solid at room temperature, and olive oil is liquid. What causes the difference?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.yazi: The shape of the fatty acids
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: The saturated fatty acids in butter have straight chains that pack tightly. In olive oil, a double bond bends the chain, so they cannot pack tightly.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Color does not decide a fat's melting point.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: Even at the same mass, one is solid and the other is liquid. The difference is in the shape of the molecules.
cards.6.p: A phospholipid has a water-loving head and two water-avoiding tails. Phospholipids line up in a double layer to form the cell membrane. Steroids are molecules with four rings. Cholesterol, estrogen, testosterone and vitamin D are steroids.
cards.6.key: Phospholipids form the framework of the cell membrane. Cholesterol keeps the fluidity of animal cell membranes steady.
cards.6.once.soru: The molecule that builds the cell membrane has one water-loving end and one water-avoiding end. There is water both inside and outside the cell. How do these molecules line up?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: The water-loving heads face the water on both sides. The water-avoiding tails turn toward each other in the middle, forming a phospholipid double layer.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The tails avoid water, so they do not face it.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The molecules do not spread randomly. The water-loving and water-avoiding ends form an orderly double layer.
cards.7.p: The building block of proteins is the amino acid, and there are 20 kinds. A peptide bond forms between amino acids as water is released. The resulting chain folds. The order of the amino acids decides the protein's shape, and its shape decides its job.
cards.7.key: Amino acid order decides folding, folding decides the 3D shape, and shape decides the job. If the shape is damaged, the protein cannot do its job.
cards.8.p: Proteins do many jobs in the body. As enzymes they speed up reactions, like keratin they form structures, and like hemoglobin they transport things. They act in defense as antibodies, as hormones such as insulin, and they make movement possible. If heat or extreme pH damages the shape (denaturation), the protein cannot do its job.
cards.8.once.soru: When an egg is cooked, the white turns opaque and firm and never goes back. What happened to the protein in the egg white?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: Heat damaged the protein's folded shape. This is called denaturation. A protein that has lost its shape cannot do its job.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Egg white is still protein. Only its shape changed.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Drying does not turn egg white opaque. Heat changed the protein's structure.
cards.9.p: The unit of nucleic acids is the nucleotide. It is made of a phosphate, a sugar and a base. DNA is double-stranded, carries the sugar deoxyribose and the bases A, T, G and C, and stores information. RNA is usually single-stranded, carries ribose, has U instead of T, and uses the information.
cards.9.key: DNA is the archive of information, and RNA is the working copy of that information.
cards.10.p: Vitamins give no energy and are needed in small amounts. Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in the body. Most water-soluble vitamins (B, C) are not stored, and any extra leaves in urine.
cards.10.svg#11: Vitamin D is also made in the skin with sunlight
cards.10.key: The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E and K.
cards.10.etk.soru: Put each vitamin in the right group: does it dissolve in fat or in water?
cards.10.etk.ogeler.1.2: Vitamin D dissolves in fat and can be stored in the body.
cards.10.etk.ogeler.4.2: Vitamin C dissolves in water. Any extra leaves in urine, so it must be taken regularly.
cards.10.etk.ogeler.6.2: B<sub>12</sub> dissolves in water. Even so, it can be stored in the liver for years.
cards.10.once.soru: For someone who takes too many vitamin pills, which is riskier?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: Vitamin A dissolves in fat and builds up in the body. Too much can cause poisoning.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Vitamin C dissolves in water, and any extra leaves in urine.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The difference is in what they dissolve in: fat-soluble ones build up, and water-soluble ones are flushed out.
cards.11.p: Substances in food are found with reagents. Iodine turns blue-black with starch. Benedict's solution turns brick red when heated with a reducing sugar. Biuret turns purple with protein. Sudan III stains fat red.
cards.11.key: Sucrose is not a reducing sugar, so it does not change the color of Benedict's solution.
cards.11.once.soru: When iodine was dropped on a potato slice, it turned blue-black. What is in the potato?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: Iodine turns blue-black with starch. A potato is the plant's starch store.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Biuret shows protein by turning purple. Iodine does not show protein.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Sudan III stains fat red. Iodine does not show fat.
cards.12.p:
• Water dissolves substances, and minerals regulate processes in the body.
• Carbohydrates give quick energy, fats are long-term storage, and phospholipids build membranes.
• Proteins form structures and do work: enzymes, transport, defense.
• Nucleic acids carry genetic information, and vitamins are regulators.
• Large molecules are built by dehydration and broken down by hydrolysis.
quiz.0.q: Put each molecule in its biomolecule group.
quiz.0.e: Starch, cellulose and lactose are carbohydrates made of sugars. Cholesterol and testosterone are steroids, and phospholipid is the lipid of membranes. Keratin and antibodies are proteins made of amino acid chains.
quiz.1.q: Match each mineral with its job in the body.
quiz.1.e: Calcium is found in bones and teeth, iron in hemoglobin, and iodine in thyroid hormone. Sodium and potassium are needed for nerve signals. Minerals give no energy. They are regulators.
quiz.2.q: 3 separate straight-chain peptides are made, each of 10 amino acids. How many water molecules are released in total?
quiz.2.e: Each chain forms 10 − 1 = 9 peptide bonds, and one water is released per bond. Across three separate chains, 3 × 9 = 27 waters are released.
quiz.3.q: Sort each structure by where it is found.
quiz.3.e: Deoxyribose and thymine are found only in DNA, and ribose and uracil only in RNA. Phosphate and the bases adenine, guanine and cytosine are found in both.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name: build and split a chain, weigh fat, damage a protein, and compare DNA with RNA.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Add glucose to build a chain of 5 glucose units, and watch what happens at each bond.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: 4 bonds formed between the 5 glucose units, and one water molecule left at each bond.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The rule is always the same: one water molecule is released for each bond.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: How many water molecules are released when a straight chain of 100 glucose units is built?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In a straight chain, the number of bonds is one less than the number of units. 100 − 1 = 99 bonds form, and 99 waters are released.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Look at the 6 glucose units on the screen and count the bonds. The number of bonds is one less than the number of units.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Water is released at every bond between two neighboring units. We are not counting the units in pairs.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Now do the reverse: add water to the chain.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: 4 waters went in, 4 bonds broke, and 5 glucose units were set free. This is how starch is split into glucose in digestion.
A:adimlar.3.metin: The bar below is the 100 kcal from 25 g of carbohydrate. How many grams of fat give the same energy? Move the slider as close to 100 kcal as you can.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 11 g of fat gives about 99 kcal. Carbohydrate needs 25 g for the same energy. Fat carries the same energy in less than half the mass. That is why fat is the long-term store.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Proteins are chains of amino acids. Change the 6th amino acid in one chain of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: What happened when a single amino acid changed?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: Its shape and job were damaged
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: This is sickle cell anemia: when valine replaces glutamic acid, hemoglobin molecules stick together. The red blood cell takes on a sickle shape, and oxygen transport suffers.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Look at what happens to the red blood cell when you change it. If the order changes, the shape can change too.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: It is still a protein. Only the amino acid order changed, and with it the shape and job.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Two molecules carry genetic information: DNA and RNA. The screen shows DNA's bases. Switch to RNA and compare the bases.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Which base is found only in RNA?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Like thymine, uracil pairs with adenine. It lacks just one methyl group compared with thymine.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Thymine is specific to DNA. Which base takes its place in RNA?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Adenine is found in both DNA and RNA.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Choose a food and a reagent, and look at the color in the tube. Show for yourself what each food contains.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.bulgular.0.tamam: Benedict's solution turned brick red when heated. So honey contains reducing sugars such as glucose and fructose.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.bulgular.1.tamam: Biuret turned purple. This color shows peptide bonds, which means protein is present.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.bulgular.2.tamam: Sudan III dissolves in fat, and a red oil layer formed on top.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.bulgular.3.yazi: Make a control tube with pure water: try a reagent.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.bulgular.3.tamam: No reagent gives a positive color with pure water. The control tube shows that the color change comes from the food.
A:adimlar.7.metin: A friend tried the same four reagents on an unknown food. Read the results.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Benedict's turned red, so there is sugar, and biuret turned purple, so there is protein. Iodine and Sudan III did not change, so starch and fat are either absent or too little for the reagent to show.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: If there were starch, iodine would turn blue-black, but the iodine stayed yellow-brown.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: If there were fat, a red layer would form with Sudan III.
A:kapanis.0: Monomers join by dehydration (releasing water), and polymers split by hydrolysis (adding water).
A:kapanis.1: In a straight chain, the number of bonds and of waters released is one less than the number of units.
A:kapanis.2: Fat gives about 9 kcal per gram and carbohydrate about 4 kcal. Fat is the long-term store.
A:kapanis.3: In a protein, amino acid order decides folding, folding decides shape, and shape decides the job. A single change can ruin the job.
A:kapanis.4: DNA is double-stranded and carries deoxyribose and the bases A, T, G and C. RNA is usually single-stranded, carries ribose, and has U instead of T.
A:kapanis.5: In food tests, iodine shows starch, Benedict's shows sugar, biuret shows protein and Sudan III shows fat. Pure water is the control tube.
